```{r}
# Loading Dependencies
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)

# Loading the Data
HealthInsurance <- read_csv("/Users/sharathchandrashankar/Downloads/health_insurance.csv")

# 1. Proportion with health insurance
n_insurance <- HealthInsurance |> filter(insurance == 'yes') |> nrow()
n <- nrow(HealthInsurance)
p_hat <- n_insurance / n
p_hat

# 2a. 95% Confidence Interval for population proportion
z <- qnorm(0.975)
se <- sqrt(p_hat * (1 - p_hat) / n)
lower <- p_hat - z * se
upper <- p_hat + z * se
c(lower = lower, upper = upper)

# 2b. Standard Error
se

# 3c. One-sample z-test for proportion
p0 <- 0.846
SE0 <- sqrt(p0 * (1 - p0) / n)
z_stat <- (p_hat - p0) / SE0
z_stat

# 3d. p-value
p_value <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_stat)))
p_value

# Part C: Self-employment and health insurance

# 1. Proportion of self-employed individuals
p_selfemp <- mean(HealthInsurance$selfemp == "yes")
p_selfemp  # Result: proportion of individuals who are self-employed

# 2. Point estimates and 95% confidence intervals for insured by employment status
insurance_by_emp <- HealthInsurance %>%
  group_by(selfemp) %>%
  summarize(
    n = n(),                          # total individuals in each group
    insured = sum(insurance == "yes"),# number with insurance
    p_hat = insured / n               # sample proportion insured
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    se = sqrt(p_hat * (1 - p_hat) / n),          # standard error
    lower = p_hat - 1.96 * se,                  # lower bound of 95% CI
    upper = p_hat + 1.96 * se                   # upper bound of 95% CI
  )

insurance_by_emp  # Result: sample proportion, standard error, and 95% CI for each group

# 3. Two-sample test for equality of proportions
table_emp <- table(HealthInsurance$selfemp, HealthInsurance$insurance)

prop_test <- prop.test(
  x = c(table_emp["yes", "yes"], table_emp["no", "yes"]),  # successes
  n = c(sum(table_emp["yes", ]), sum(table_emp["no", ])), # total per group
  correct = FALSE                                         # no continuity correction
)

prop_test  # Result: chi-squared test statistic, p-value, confidence interval
```
